rationale: Retain the source protection against stale snapshot completion clearing a newer pending snapshot; distinguish it from cross-worker application ordering.

feedback.answered: The old-completion/new-snapshot suspicion is explained by complementary source protections. Full restore immediately sets committed to its snapshot index; restore rejects any subsequent snapshot at or below committed. Therefore a later accepted replacement has a strictly larger index. stableSnapTo only clears an exact index match, so an earlier response, including one accepted across a term change, leaves the newer snapshot pending. appliedSnap uses max(oldApplied, completedIndex) and does not restore the old ConfState. promotable and committed-entry delivery inspect the remaining pending/in-progress snapshot, preserving their block until its own completion. A matching-log snapshot instead fast-forwards commit without installing a replacement. These are code-derived relationships, not new execution Evidence or a proof of recovery correctness.
remaining: Next discriminator: examine the embedding contract for ordering an outstanding MsgStorageApply batch against a newer snapshot handled by LocalAppendThread. The two local destinations may progress independently; determine which layer owns state-machine snapshot/application coordination before proposing a check.
feedback.rationale: Snapshot identity and monotonic commit settle the selected stale-marker question without a synthetic execution. The independent local-worker boundary is a different responsibility: a preserved pending marker does not itself establish correct external state-machine ordering. Source duties must determine its applicability first.
